'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Aftermath of the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]] and [[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
***The [[United States]] will contribute [[United States dollar|$]]64 million to the [[United Nations]]' famine prevention effort in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/middle-east-north-africa/572038-us-sending-64m-in-humanitarian-aid-to (The Hill)]
***[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] defends the [[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|U.S. withdrawal]] during a testimony congressional hearing. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghanistan-blame-game-shifts-us-congress-blinken-testifies-2021-09-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2021 Niger attacks]]
***A report by [[Amnesty International]] citing other organizations says that an increasing number of children are being killed and abducted as the conflict in [[Niger]], mainly in the [[Tillabéri Region]], worsens near the border with [[Mali]] and [[Burkina Faso]]. The report says that "a generation is growing surrounded by death and destruction" and denounces "gross abuses" by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] and [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]]. The report urges the [[government of Niger|government]] and international partners to "take action". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/13/armed-groups-killing-recruiting-more-children-in-niger-amnesty (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**[[Bello Matawalle]], the [[List of governors of Zamfara State|Governor]] of [[Zamfara State]], [[Nigeria]], announces that 68 children who were abducted two weeks ago have been rescued by [[Nigerian Armed Forces|Nigerian forces]] and reunited with their families. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/authorities-70-students-freed-northern-nigeria-79987698 (AP via ABC News)]
*[[Panjshir conflict]]
**The [[BBC]] documents and reports that the [[Taliban]] deliberately targeted civilians in [[Panjshir Province]] despite promises to avoid retaliatory attacks on local civilians. One of the documented cases was that of a shopkeeper as the news agency says that up to 20 civilians were killed by Taliban fighters during their advance on the last anti-Taliban stronghold. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58545892 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*Aftermath of the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]]
**[[Pakistan International Airlines]] operates the first international commercial flight to [[Kabul International Airport]] since [[Kabul|the city]]'s takeover by the [[Taliban]] on August 15. [https://mb.com.ph/2021/09/13/first-foreign-commercial-flight-since-taliban-takeover-lands-in-kabul-afp/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
**The [[United Nations]] begins a fundraising event to collect [[United States dollar|$]]600 million in emergency funds for various Afghani agencies by the end of the year. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2021/09/13/un-afghanistan-aid-taliban/8361631535754/ (UPI)]
*A [[Netherlands|Dutch]] court rules that [[Uber]] drivers are entitled to the same employee benefits afforded to [[taxi]] drivers. The court also orders the company to pay a [[Euro|€]]50,000 fine for damages. [https://www.usnews.com/news/business/articles/2021-09-13/dutch-court-uber-drivers-covered-by-taxi-labor-agreement (AP via ''U.S. News and World Report'')] [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/08/04/uber-earnings-q2-2021.html (CNBC)]
*[[United States|American]] international [[Credit bureau|consumer credit reporting agency]] [[TransUnion]] agrees to purchase American technology company [[Neustar]] for [[United States dollar|$]]3.1 billion. [https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/transunion-buys-neustar-expand-digital-marketing (Fox Business)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Greece]]
*****The [[Greece|Greek]] [[Ministry of Health (Greece)|Health ministry]] approves [[booster dose]]s of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for people over the age of 60 years and people with a [[Immunocompromise|compromised immune]] system. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/1167820/experts-approve-booster-covid-19-shot-for-those-over-60-vulnerable/ (Ekathimerini)]
****Greece begins to implement mandatory weekly [[COVID-19 testing]] for unvaccinated people. Public and private employees are required to pay for tests for their unvaccinated employees while unvaccinated high school students will be given test kits distributed at the [[Government of Greece|government]]'s expense. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/09/13/greece-begins-mandatory-testing-for-unvaccinated-workers (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
*****The [[United Kingdom]] cancels a deal to purchase [[Valneva COVID-19 vaccine|vaccines developed]] by [[Valneva SE]] following accusations of breaching the agreement. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-58499064 (BBC News)]
*****The four [[Chief Medical Officers (United Kingdom)|Chief Medical Officers]] recommend universal COVID-19 vaccination for children aged 12 to 15 years using the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] in order to reduce the possible disruption to schools. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/13/uk-children-aged-12-to-15-to-be-offered-covid-jab (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania]]
****[[Lithuania]] restricts the access of non-essential shops, gyms, beauty services, or events attended by more than 500 people, to only those who have a National Certificate proving that they have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Lithuania|vaccinated]], have tested negative, or who have recovered from COVID-19. [https://m.delfi.lt/en/article.php?id=88171727 (Delfi)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo]]
****[[President of the Democratic Republic of Congo|President]] [[Félix Tshisekedi]] receives his first dose of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.news24.com/news24/africa/news/after-being-unwilling-congo-president-felix-tshisekedi-gets-his-covid-19-jab-20210913 (News24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[South Africa]] moves to adjusted level 2 restrictions that will allow licensed establishments to serve alcohol until 10 p.m. Additionally, the curfew will begin one hour later at 11 p.m. [https://www.businessinsider.co.za/new-level-2-means-two-hours-extra-boozing-time-at-shebeens-and-bars-regulations-confirm-2021-9 (''Business Insider South Africa'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement]]
****[[Indonesia]] moves the level of the PPKM in [[Bali]] to level 3 and will also allow visitors to enter parts of the island as long as they adhere to strict health protocols. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/indonesia-eases-covid-19-restrictions-in-bali-borders-to-be-tightened (Reuters via ''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports 607 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since August 2020. [https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/new-covid-19-cases-sept-13-21 (''Today'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 41 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.wftv.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-41-million/LP7S2JCSJFBABJBSLX3YJ2YWBY/ (WFTV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
*****[[Education in New York City|Schools]] in [[New York City]] reopen for the first time since the start of the [[pandemic]] in March 2020. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/13/nyregion/nyc-schools-reopening.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
****[[New South Wales]] eases its [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown rules]] for people who have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|vaccinated]] against COVID-19 where people outside [[Local government areas of New South Wales|LGA]]s of concern are allowed to gather in groups of up to five people in a person's LGA or within {{cvt|5|km}} from their home. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-09-13/restrictions-ease-for-fully-vaccinated-nsw-residents-explained/100455200 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sierra Leone]]
***[[Sierra Leone]] ends its nationwide 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. [[curfew]] that had been in place since July due to declining number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.switsalone.com/39689_sierra-leone-lifts-its-nationwide-curfew-as-the-countrys-covid-19-cases-reduce-%EF%BB%BF/ (Switsalone)]

'''International relations'''
*[[List of North Korean missile tests|North Korean missile tests]]
**[[North Korea]] confirms it has tested a new long-range [[cruise missile]] capable of carrying a [[nuclear weapon|nuclear warhead]]. The missiles are a "strategic weapon of great significance", according to [[Korean Central News Agency|state media]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-58540915 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Emily Claire Hari, the leader of an [[Illinois]]-based, anti-government militia group, is sentenced to 53 years in prison for masterminding the August 2017 bombing of the [[Dar Al-Farooq Islamic Center]] in [[Bloomington, Minnesota]]. [https://apnews.com/article/religion-crime-minnesota-illinois-hate-crimes-3a1819d8ea489a6a9485e60a800c0824 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020–21 Malaysian political crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Ismail Sabri Yaakob]] and the [[Leader of the Opposition (Malaysia)|Leader of the Opposition]] [[Anwar Ibrahim]] of the main opposition coalition [[Pakatan Harapan]] sign a [[confidence and supply]] agreement ending the 18-month political crisis that has led to the fall of two successive governments. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysian-government-and-opposition-pakatan-harapan-ink-historic-mou-bipartisan-cooperation-2174116 (CNA)]
*[[2021 Norwegian parliamentary election]]
**[[Norwegians]] go to the polls to elect the new [[Storting]]. The opposition [[Labour Party (Norway)|Labour Party]] led by [[Jonas Gahr Støre]] wins the most seats and is expected to form a [[Left-wing politics|left-wing]]-dominated government. The [[Centre Party (Norway)|Centre Party]], [[Red Party (Norway)|Red Party]], [[Socialist Left Party (Norway)|Socialist Left Party]] and [[Green Party (Norway)|Green Party]] also gained seats. [[Prime Minister of Norway|Prime Minister]] [[Erna Solberg]] concedes defeat. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/winner-norways-election-is-wealthy-champion-common-people-2021-09-13/ (Reuters)]
